title: International School Teacher Pedagogy in Managing the Behavior of Students from Different Cultures
abstract: The low ability of teachers to manage student behavior impacts the effectiveness of learning. The urgency of improving teachers' pedagogical competence in behavior management creates a conducive and inclusive learning atmosphere. The aim is to analyze the level of knowledge and skills of teachers in managing student behavior based on gender, age, and race variables. The quantitative approach method with a survey design of 160 teachers internationally. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire (1–5) and analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, and One-Way ANOVA with the help of SPSS 29.0. The results show a high level of teacher knowledge (average 4.71 out of 5), with significant differences based on gender (t = 2.621; p = 0.011), but not significant based on age (F = 0.563; p = 0.802) or race (F = 3.356; p = 0.190). The findings highlight the importance of ongoing training in positive behavior management. Conclusion: Improving teacher competence through training and strengthening learning modules is key to the effectiveness of student behavior management. Implications: Schools need to develop behavior management training policies based on inclusive practices.

title: The Effectiveness of the Kurikulum Cinta Grounded in Social Emotional Learning in Enhancing Students’ Character in Elementary School Hindu Religious Education
abstract: Character education in Hindu Religious Education at elementary schools still faces challenges in systematically integrating character development and social-emotional competencies because learning focuses more on cognitive aspects than meaningful affective and behavioral dimension. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness and analyze the acceptance of the Kurikulum Cinta grounded in Social Emotional Learning (SEL) in enhancing students’ character in Hindu Religious Education. The study employed a mixed-methods design involving one Hindu Religious Education teacher and 32 elementary school students. Data were collected through classroom observations, interviews, document analysis, and character assessment instruments that had met content and construct validity requirements, with a reliability coefficient of 0.769. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative data were interpreted thematically. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) was also employed to examine teacher acceptance of the learning model. The findings revealed improvements in students’ learning engagement, emotional awareness, reflective abilities, and respectful attitudes. In addition, the mode

title: Development of Interactive Multimedia Based Learning Media for Petanque Sports Extracurricular Development Course
abstract: The limited availability of interactive and contextual learning media in the Petanque Sports Extracurricular Development course has hindered the optimization of student engagement and learning outcomes. This study aimed to develop, evaluate the feasibility of, and examine the effectiveness of interactive digital multimedia-based learning media to improve the quality of petanque instruction. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the Borg and Gall model. The research subjects included subject matter experts, media experts, petanque experts, and students involved in the small group, large group, and operational field trials. Data were collected through expert validation questionnaires, student response questionnaires, and learning achievement tests, and were analyzed using qualitative descriptive analysis, quantitative descriptive analysis, and the Independent Samples t-test. The results indicated that the developed learning media was rated as good during the initial validation and improved to excellent after revision. Student responses increased from 82.53% in the small-group trial to 92.33% in the large-group trial. The t-test results revealed a signific

title: Parenting Styles of Single Parents and the Foundation of Social and Emotional Development in Early Childhood
abstract: The increasing number of single parent families highlights the need to understand how parenting within such family structures influences the development of early childhood social competence and emotional stability. This study aims to analyze and explore the impact of single parent caregiving on children’s social competence and emotional stability across different cultural contexts. A qualitative approach with a phenomenological design was employed to examine the influence of single parent parenting on early childhood social competence and emotional stability in various cultural backgrounds. The study involved 12 children aged 5-8 years raised in single parent families. Data were collected through participant observation, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions using semi structured interview guides and observation protocols. Data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles and Huberman, which includes data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings show that children in single parent families exhibit variations in social competence and emotional stability despite the application of democratic parenting, influenced by caregiver rol

title: SAMRATED: A Conceptual Integration of SAMR and SDT to Evaluate Digital Transformation in Higher Education Learning
abstract: The integration of digital technology in higher education continues to expand; however, its implementation is often limited to the digitization of learning materials, resulting in suboptimal improvements in students’ motivation and learning outcomes. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of e-module utilization in enhancing students’ learning outcomes and intrinsic motivation through the integration of the Substitution, Augmentation, Modification, Redefinition (SAMR) framework and Self-Determination Theory (SDT). A mixed-methods approach with a quasi-experimental design was employed, involving 247 undergraduate students divided into an experimental group (e-module) and a control group (e-book). Data were collected through learning achievement tests, SAMR–SDT-based motivation questionnaires, and classroom observations, and were analyzed using nonparametric statistical tests and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results revealed that students who used the e-module demonstrated greater improvements in learning outcomes than those who used the e-book. Structural model analysis further indicated that the redefinition dimension was the most influent

title: Google Docs Utilization in Collaborative Academic Text Writing: Student Perceptions of Ease of Use, Barriers, and Continuity of Use
abstract: Technological developments have brought about online based collaborative learning through Google Docs, which needs to be analyzed and evaluated regarding the effectiveness of its use in academic text writing. This study aims to analyze, evaluate, and explore students’ interpretations of the use of Google Docs in collaborative writing activities using a qualitative approach and a phenomenological perspective. Data were collected from 13 students through semi structured interviews and then analyzed thematically to construct meanings from their experiences of using the technology. The analysis resulted in four main themes of students’ perceptions of Google Docs. The first, Perceived Ease of Use, includes ease of use, free access, and flexibility. The second, Perceived Usefulness, covers collaborative writing support, learning to write, editing, and accelerating the writing process. The third, Perceived Barriers, includes unfamiliar group members, low responsiveness among members, and limitations when using smartphones. title: Analysis of the Influence of Socioeconomic Status on Smartphone Use Restrictions in Early Childhood: A Digital Parenting Survey Study
abstract: Parents’ socioeconomic status (SES) is a key factor influencing how they regulate and supervise young children’s smartphone use. This study aimed to analyze differences in parental restriction methods based on SES. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 115 parents of children aged 3–6 years enrolled in kindergartens and early childhood education centers (TK/PAUD) through purposive sampling. Inclusion criteria required that the child had used a smartphone for at least six months. Data were gathered online via Google Forms and analyzed using the Chi-square test to examine associations between SES categories and restriction methods. The results showed that conventional restriction methods were more commonly applied than digital ones across all education and occupation groups. Chi-square analysis indicated significant differences between SES and the restriction methods employed. Parents with higher SES tended to use digital features such as parental control and screen time monitoring, whereas those with lower SES relied on direct communication and physical supervision. title: The Effectiveness of Canva-Based Animated Video Media in Pancasila Education Learning: The Bhinneka Tunggal Ika Element fot Grade V Elementary School Students
abstract: The limited use of innovative instructional media in Pancasila Education has reduced students’ learning engagement and hindered their understanding of the values of Bhinneka Tunggal Ika. Conventional teacher-centered learning practices often fail to provide meaningful and interactive learning experiences, resulting in less optimal learning outcomes in elementary schools. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of Canva-based animated video media in improving students’ learning outcomes in the Bhinneka Tunggal Ika element of Pancasila Education. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model, consisting of the analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation stages. The research involved 68 fifth-grade elementary school students, who participated in limited trials, implementation, and dissemination stages. Data were collected through pretest and posttest learning achievement tests and analyzed using the normalized gain (N-Gain) method to evaluate learning improvement after the implementation of the developed media. The findings indicate that the Canva-based animated video media produced a moderate and sufficiently effective impr

title: The Activeness and Learning Motivation of MTs Ibnu Sina Students in Ecoprint Learning Using Project-Based Learning Modules
abstract: Skill-based learning often faces challenges related to low student motivation and limited engagement in the learning process. This study aims to analyze students’ learning activity and learning motivation in ecoprint learning using a Project-Based Learning (PBL)-based module, as well as to explore factors that support student engagement during the learning process. The study employed a quantitative descriptive approach involving 25 eighth-grade students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a learning activity self-assessment instrument, a learning motivation questionnaire, an open-ended questionnaire, and documentation. Instrument validity was tested using Pearson’s Correlation, while reliability was examined using Cronbach’s Alpha. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics with high, moderate, and low categories. The findings revealed that most students demonstrated high and moderate levels of learning activity, while learning motivation was predominantly categorized as high. No students were classified in the low category for either aspect. Qualitative findings indicated that affective factors, hands-on activities, and creative-artistic elements we

title: Development of a Rhythmic Gymnastics Learning Model to Improve the Motor Skills of Students with Mild Intellectual Disabilities
abstract: Students with mild intellectual disabilities often experience limitations in motor development, particularly in coordination, balance, flexibility, and movement control, which affect their participation in physical education learning. Existing learning practices tend to rely on conventional instructional approaches and have not optimally accommodated the characteristics and learning needs of students with intellectual disabilities. This study aimed to develop, analyze, and evaluate the effectiveness of a rhythmic gymnastics learning model in improving the motor skills of students with mild intellectual disabilities. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model, which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The research involved 30 students with mild intellectual disabilities, while data were collected through observation, expert validation questionnaires, motor skill assessment sheets, and documentation. The developed instruments were validated by experts before implementation, and the collected quantitative and qualitative data were analyzed descriptively to evaluate the feasibility and effectivene

title: An Empirical Study of Reading Comprehension Levels among Elementary School Students Based on Barrett's Taxonomy Framework
abstract: Fifth-grade elementary students still show suboptimal reading comprehension, particularly in understanding informative texts that are essential for academic success. This descriptive quantitative study aims to analyze the reading comprehension of 30 fifth-grade students using Barrett’s Taxonomy Framework and cluster random sampling. Data were collected using a standardized comprehension test covering all five levels of Barrett’s taxonomy; literal, reorganization, inferential, evaluative, and appreciative and analyzed descriptively using SPSS 25. Findings revealed 40% of students were “less competent.” Evaluative comprehension showed the highest proficiency (76.9%), while reorganization was weakest (66.3%). Overall, most students (63.3%) fell into low and medium categories by Azwar’s classification, indicating significant difficulties in higher-order comprehension skills like inference and information restructuring. These results align with theoretical frameworks such as Vygotsky’s Zone of Proximal Development and Bandura’s Social Cognitive Theory, underscoring the crucial role of scaffolding and self-efficacy in reading development. title: Reconstruction of the Axiological Values of the Ngerateng Lampad Tradition for the Development of a Holistic Character Education Model
abstract: Tradition plays an important role in shaping cultural identity and transmitting values; however, globalization and digitalization have encouraged a shift toward individualism and weakened authentic social interactions, contributing to the moral degradation of younger generations. This condition necessitates the reconstruction of character education that is contextual and rooted in local wisdom. This study aims to analyze the axiological values of character education embedded in the Ngerateng Lampad tradition as a reconstruction of local wisdom for contemporary holistic education. The study employed a descriptive qualitative method with an ethnographic approach involving traditional leaders, youth groups, community leaders, and community members who support the tradition. Data were collected through observation, in depth interviews, documentation, and questionnaires, and were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model, with validity ensured through triangulation and member checking. The findings reveal that the Ngerateng Lampad tradition embodies religious-spiritual values, mutual cooperation, responsibility, environmental awareness, perseverance, discipline, creativity, and wisdom

title: Contextual Learning-Oriented Animated Cartoons on Student Learning Outcomes in Mathematics Subjects
abstract: Mathematics is a fundamental subject that plays an important role in developing elementary school students' critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. Students' perceptions of mathematics as a difficult, boring, and uninteresting subject remain a challenge, resulting in low learning motivation and achievement. This study aimed to develop and analyze the validity, practicality, and effectiveness of a 2D Animated Cartoon learning media based on Contextual Learning for the topic of whole number operations among second-grade elementary school students. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) and involved 30 second grade students as the trial participants. Data were collected through questionnaires and tests using rating scale assessment sheets and pretest–posttest instruments, and were analyzed using qualitative descriptive and quantitative descriptive techniques. The findings indicated that the 2D Animated Cartoon learning media based on Contextual Learning met the criteria of validity, practicality, and effectiveness, thereby improving students' mathematics learn

title: Optimization of the Belajar.id Account to Enhance 21st-Century Teacher Competence
abstract: The transformation of 21st century education requires teachers to possess adaptive pedagogical, professional, social, and technological competencies; however, the utilization of learning technology by teachers is still not optimal. This study aims to analyze the optimization of the Belajar.id account in improving teacher competence through independent self-development, technology integration, and the use of digital platforms connected to educational services. This research employs a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted through coding, categorization, and theme identification, and its validity was tested through source triangulation. The findings show that the Belajar.id account contributes to improving teacher competence, particularly in accessing independent training, developing innovative teaching materials using Canva for Education, and utilizing the Ruang GTK/PMM platform for reflection and professional development. title: Development of SciSpark Learning Media in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) to Optimize Critical Thinking in Elementary Schools
abstract: The limited use of interactive learning media in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) instruction has resulted in low student engagement and insufficient development of critical thinking skills. Existing classroom practices remain predominantly teacher-centered and textbook-based, limiting opportunities for higher-order thinking. This study aimed to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of SciSpark, an interactive digital learning medium designed to enhance elementary school students’ critical thinking skills in IPAS learning. The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) model, combined with a quasi-experimental design. The participants were elementary school students assigned to experimental and control groups. Data were collected through classroom observations, teacher interviews, expert validation sheets, critical thinking tests, and student response questionnaires. Data analysis included expert validity assessment, descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test, and N-Gain analysis to measure improvements in students’ critical thinking skills. title: Innovative Gamification in the Digital Age: Improving Reading Comprehension Elementary School Students
abstract: In the digital era, elementary school students continue to face challenges in reading comprehension due to low learning motivation and the predominance of conventional instructional approaches that provide limited opportunities for interactive learning. These conditions highlight the need for innovative instructional strategies capable of enhancing students' engagement in reading activities. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of gamification in improving elementary school students' reading comprehension skills. A quantitative approach employing a One-Group Pretest–Posttest experimental design was adopted, involving 38 fifth-grade students as the research participants. Data were collected using a validated and reliable multiple-choice reading comprehension test and analyzed through descriptive and inferential statistics, including the paired-samples t-test using SPSS. The findings revealed that the implementation of gamification significantly improved students' reading comprehension skills. The integration of game elements, such as points, levels, and challenges, enhanced students' engagement, motivation, and active participation, making the reading process more meaningful

title: Fostering Critical Thinking Skills through Project-Based Learning and Learning Motivation in Local History Education
abstract: Developing students' critical thinking skills remains a major challenge in higher education history learning, particularly due to the dominance of teacher-centered instruction and limited attention to learning motivation. This condition results in superficial understanding and low levels of higher-order cognitive engagement. Therefore, this study aims to analyze and evaluate the contribution of Project-Based Learning (PjBL) and learning motivation to the enhancement of students’ critical thinking skills in local history education. The study involved 71 undergraduate students enrolled in a history education program. Data were collected through critical thinking skills tests, learning motivation questionnaires, and classroom observation sheets to examine the implementation of PjBL. All instruments were validated by experts prior to use. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics and inferential analysis, including paired samples t-test, independent samples t-test, Mixed Between-Within ANOVA, and linear regression analysis. title: The Effectiveness of an Ethno Project-Based Teaching Module Integrated with Technology in Basic Culinary Learning to Improve Vocational High School Students’ Learning Interest
abstract: Learning in culinary vocational education at vocational high schools is still predominantly characterized by conventional teacher-centered methods, resulting in suboptimal student engagement in the learning process. In addition, the limited use of educational technology and the lack of integration of local culinary cultural contexts contribute to students' low learning interest in Basic Culinary subjects, as indicated by low enthusiasm, participation, and learning independence. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of an Ethno Project-Based Teaching Module integrated with technology in improving students' learning interest in Basic Culinary subjects at vocational high schools. The study employed a pre-experimental design with a pretest-posttest control group, involving 33 students divided into two groups: an experimental group that used a technology-integrated ethno-culinary project-based module and a control group that received conventional learning instruction. The results showed a significant improvement in students’ learning interest in the experimental group after the implementation of the module, as indicated by a significant difference between pretest and posttest sc

title: Needs Analysis for Developing a STEM Based E-LKPD Integrated with PjBL to Enhance Students’ Cognitive Learning Outcomes in Elementary Mathematics
abstract: Socioeconomic changes and advances in information technology in the era of globalization require elementary school graduates to master 21st-century skills (7C). The Merdeka Curriculum encourages conceptual and contextual mathematics learning, including number patterns in Phase B. However, a gap remains between curriculum demands, digital media availability, and teachers’ pedagogical readiness. This study aims to analyze the needs for developing STEM based E-LKPD integrated with Project Based Learning (PjBL) to improve learning quality. This research uses a mixed method approach with a descriptive design. The research subjects consist of three mathematics teachers as interview informants and 33 teachers as survey respondents, with teaching module documents as supporting data sources. Data were collected through semi structured interviews, questionnaires, and document analysis, then analyzed using thematic analysis and descriptive statistics. The results show that learning is still dominated by conventional methods, with limited application of STEM and limited development of digital teaching materials. title: Development of QR Code-Based Big Book Media to Improve the Literacy Skills of Elementary School Students in Phase A
abstract: The low literacy skills of Phase A students are a real challenge in elementary schools, supported by the limited interactive and contextual learning media. This study aims to (1) analyze the need for media development, (2) develop a prototype of QR Code-based BigBook media, and (3) test its effectiveness in improving literacy skills. The subjects of the study were 47 students and 3 teachers from three public elementary schools in Madiun City. Data were collected through expert validation sheets, literacy tests (pre-test and post-test), observations, and questionnaires. The instruments were analyzed descriptively quantitatively, followed by paired sample t-tests and N-Gain calculations. The results of expert validation of material, media, and language obtained an average percentage of 94.28% (Very Feasible category). title: Ecological Perspective: The Role of English Teachers at Private Elite Elementary Schools
abstract: Learning is viewed as an ecological system consisting of many components inside and outside classroom which interrelated and dependent on each other. The ecology in roles of teachers is a lens that shows that all elements are interconnected to help to understand their roles from a holistic perspective. Thus, the purpose of the study is to analyze how the ecological context shaped the role of teachers at a religion-based school and an inclusive school. In this research, a qualitative multiple-case study involving purposive cross-case comparison sampling technique was employed to select principals, English teachers, homeroom teachers, and students of two private elite elementary schools. Data can be obtained through observation, semi-structured interview, students open-ended questionnaire, and document analysis. The activities in data analysis are data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing/verification. This study demonstrates that English teachers both at A and B Elementary Schools play the similar roles as controller, director, and facilitator. title: Need Assessment of Deep Learning to Improve Critical-Innovative Thinking Abilities from the Perspective of Master Program Students
abstract: The demands of 21st-century education require university students to possess strong critical and innovative thinking skills. However, theoretical learning in higher education remains predominantly conventional, resulting in limited opportunities for students to construct knowledge deeply. This study aims to analyze and evaluate the effectiveness of a deep learning approach in enhancing critical and innovative thinking skills among master's level students. The research employed a convergent parallel mixed-methods design, involving 46 graduate students as research participants. Data were collected using a mixed-form questionnaire consisting of closed-ended and open-ended items, supported by documentation. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively using percentages, while qualitative responses were interpreted thematically. The results indicate that theoretical learning still lacks variation and consistency, yet 93.5% of students reported that deep learning fosters critical thinking and 87% agreed that it encourages innovative thinking, although only 45.7% frequently apply both during coursework. title: The The Role of Scaffolding in Optimizing Problem-Based Learning to Develop Students' Critical Thinking Skills
abstract: In the 2015 TIMSS, Indonesian students scored 397, ranking 44th out of 49 countries. This data suggests that Indonesian students consistently lack critical thinking skills in mathematics. The purpose of this study was to investigate the role of scaffolding within a Problem-Based Learning (PBL) framework in enhancing the critical thinking skills of junior high school students. This study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design, which involved one experimental group. For this study, a random sample of 27 eighth-grade students was selected. Data were collected using a critical thinking test evaluated through an essay test created based on criteria established by Facione. Data analysis was carried out descriptively and inferentially. The data normality test, using the Shapiro Wilk test, showed that most of the data were not normally distributed; therefore, the inferential analysis was continued with the nonparametric Wilcoxon Signed Ranks Test. Data processing was conducted using SPSS software version 30.0. title: The The Effectiveness of a Pancasila-Based Interactive Physical Education Module in Enhancing Elementary School Students' Character Values
abstract: Physical Education in elementary schools still focuses on achieving motor skills, while the integration of Pancasila values has not been optimally implemented. This condition has an impact on the potential for character building through physical activity, which should be an essential part of the educational process, and is not maximized. This study aims to develop and test the effectiveness of an interactive Pancasila-based Physical Education module for elementary school students, ensuring that learning not only emphasizes physical aspects but also values and character. The research method employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach, utilizing the ADDIE model. The needs analysis involved 18 Physical Education teachers in North Sumatra. The research data analysis employed a mixed-methods approach that combines quantitative and qualitative data. The results showed that 72.2% of teachers stated they really need an interactive character-based module, 11.1% said they need it, 11.1% stated they do not need it, and 5.6% stated they do not need it. title: Booklet ‘Pakuli to Kaili’: An Innovative Civics Learning Media Utilizing Local Wisdom to Enhance the Pancasila Student Profile
abstract: The main challenge in Civic Education lies in the weak integration of Pancasila values with local wisdom, which results in low students’ awareness of cultural identity, particularly the local wisdom of the Kaili ethnic group. This study aims to develop and evaluate the Pakuli To Kaili booklet as an innovative and contextual learning medium. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model. The participants consisted of 35 students, 2 teachers, and 1 media expert as a validator. Data were collected through interviews, observation checklists, expert validation sheets, and student–teacher questionnaires. Instrument validity was analyzed using item–total correlation and reliability using Cronbach’s Alpha, while overall data were analyzed descriptively. Expert validation instruments were used to assess the feasibility of the Pakuli To Kaili booklet as a local wisdom–based Civic Education learning medium. The instruments were designed in the form of a four-point Likert-scale questionnaire (1–4), covering content feasibility, language, presentation, and media design aspects. title: Enhancing Pre Service Teachers TPACK through Reusable Learning Object-Based Blended Learning: A Comparative Study of Pre-Service Teachers with Diverse Self-Regulated Learning
abstract: The main issue is the lack of adequate resources and training for teachers, which affects the ability of curriculum developers to design effective strategies for both teachers and students. This study aims to examine the perspectives of curriculum developers on the obstacles encountered in the implementation of differentiated learning curriculum. The research uses a phenomenological method to explore information based on the direct experiences of curriculum developers. Data collection was conducted through in-depth interviews with 6 primary school teachers from the Penggerak School program. The collected data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify key patterns emerging from their experiences. The results show that the integration of differentiated learning curriculum can be achieved through diagnostic assessment, teaching modules, or adjustments in teaching techniques by the teachers. The study also finds that differentiated learning is currently understood as a hidden curriculum, referring to elements not included in the official curriculum but still applied in teaching practices. title: The Effectiveness of the PanduHaid Application in Improving Independent Skills of Students with Mild Intellectual Disabilities During Menstruation
abstract: The limited independent ability of children with mild intellectual disabilities in managing menstrual hygiene presents a significant challenge in developing their self-reliance. The scarcity of adaptive learning media tailored to the cognitive characteristics of these children exacerbates this issue. This study aims to design, develop, and evaluate the effectiveness of the PanduHaid application as an interactive learning tool to enhance the independent menstrual hygiene management skills of children with mild intellectual disabilities. The research subjects consisted of several students with mild intellectual disabilities who were tested using a Research and Development (R&D) approach based on the ADDIE model. Data were collected through pretest-posttest instruments and expert validation, then analyzed quantitatively using the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test. The results demonstrated that the PanduHaid application is highly valid and practical, with an Aiken’s V value > 0.90 and practicality score of 0.908, and effectively improved students' independent skills significantly (Z = -2.032, p = 0.042, r = 0.91). title: Building Imaginative Character through Musical Storytelling Methods to Enhance Elementary School Students’ Creativity
abstract: Learning in elementary schools still tends to use teacher-centered learning methods with an approach that emphasizes memorization and reproduction of information. This can hinder the development of students' creativity and imagination. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of the musical storytelling method in enhancing the imaginative character and creativity of elementary school students. The research method used is a quasi-experiment with a static group pretest-posttest design. The sample was selected using purposive sampling. The experimental class and control class each consisted of 15 students. Data collection instruments used tests. Data analysis techniques used quantitative and qualitative analysis. The results of the t-test analysis showed that there was a significant difference between the experimental class and the control class. The average post-test score of the experimental class after the treatment was 85, while the average post-test score of the control class was 80. title: The “Susuka” Application to Improve Sentence-Building Learning for Deaf Students
abstract: Sentence construction is an essential aspect of language and communication development. However, students with hearing disabilities often struggle to form complete sentence structures due to the limited availability of learning media tailored to their needs and characteristics. This study aims to develop SuSuKa (Susun Susun Kalimat), an educational game-based application designed to support sentence construction skills among students with hearing disabilities. The research employed a Research and Development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model, which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The participants were five elementary school students with hearing disabilities. The SuSuKa application was validated by two experts, namely an expert in hearing disability education and an instructional media expert, while practicality was assessed by teachers. Effectiveness was measured through pretest and posttest assessments of sentence construction skills. The findings showed that SuSuKa was highly valid (Aiken’s V > 0.90), rated highly practical by teachers (0.908), and effective in enhancing sentence construction skills. The Wilcoxon Signed-Ra

title: The Jogja Library Center Tour: Literacy-Based Inquiry Model to Improve Historical Thinking Skill
abstract: A pedagogical approach dominated by a single narrative often neglects the analysis of sources, context, and causal relationships in history. This weakens students' historical literacy skills, thereby affecting their ability to develop practical historical thinking skills. The purpose of this study is to analyze the implementation of the Jogja Library Center Tour inquiry model in history learning, which utilizes old daily newspapers to improve historical Literacy and its implications for improving historical thinking skills. This study used a qualitative method with a case study approach. The subjects were the Deputy Head of the Library Center. The school curriculum field consisted of one person, a history teacher, and three representatives from class XII students. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and document analysis, utilizing the Miles and Huberman interactive model analysis technique. Data were analyzed using Miles and Huberman's interactive analysis model, which includes the stages of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion. title: Flash Card Palindrome (FCPM): Critical Thinking Skills Stimulation Media to Support Early Childhood Education Curriculum in the Globalization Era
abstract: Early childhood often experiences difficulties in developing critical thinking skills due to the lack of engaging, contextual learning media that meet the curriculum demands in the globalization era. The unavailability of innovative stimulation media such as Flash Card Palindrome (FCPM) results in the learning process being less able to optimize children's cognitive potential in recognizing patterns, analyzing information, and solving simple problems. This study aims to determine the effectiveness of flash card palindrome (FCPM) media in improving critical thinking skills in children aged 5–6 years. The study employed a quantitative approach, utilizing a quasi-experimental method with an equivalent time series design, involving a sample of 13 children. Data were obtained through observation and analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test because the data did not meet the assumption of normal distribution. The results showed a significant difference in critical thinking skills between posttest 1 and posttest 5 after treatment using FCPM. title: Students’ Thought Process in Solving Inverse Proportion Problem in Terms of Cognitive Style and Gender Based on Information Processing Theory
abstract: Students’ ability to solve inverse proportion problems remains low due to difficulties in understanding variable relationships, indicating differences in thinking processes related to cognitive styles and gender. This study aimed to analyze, compare, and evaluate students’ thinking processes in solving inverse proportion problems based on cognitive style and gender using an information-processing theoretical framework. This research employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive-exploratory design. The research subjects consisted of eight eighth-grade students selected purposively, representing Field Independent (FI) and Field Dependent (FD) cognitive styles as well as male and female students. Data were collected through written mathematical problem-solving tests and in-depth interviews as the main research instruments. The data were analyzed using interactive qualitative data analysis. The findings revealed that differences in students’ thinking processes were more strongly influenced by cognitive style than by gender, in line with the primary objective of the study. title: An Integrative Character Education Model in English Language Learning for High School Students
abstract: The development of character education requires teachers to be able to effectively integrate moral values and virtues into the learning process. However, implementing the right strategies in English language learning remains a challenge in many schools. This study aims to analyze teachers' strategies in integrating character values into English language learning. A qualitative approach with a case study method was used to explore in depth the teaching practices of six English teachers. Data were collected through analysis of lesson plans, classroom observations, and in-depth interviews, then analyzed using thematic analysis techniques. The results show that teachers apply character integration in a planned, contextual, and sustainable manner through problem-based learning, open discussions, role-play, community projects, and value reflection. Conceptually, this study confirms that value-based integrative strategies can strengthen language proficiency while shaping students' social and moral character. title: Articulate Storyline Learning Media with Gimkit Respiratory System Material to Improve Critical Thinking Skills
abstract: Learning in elementary schools still shows low levels of students’ critical thinking skills due to the dominance of teacher-centered instruction and the suboptimal use of learning media. This condition causes students to rely on memorization and limits their ability to analyze and solve contextual problems. This study aims to analyze, design, and evaluate the development of interactive learning media using Articulate Storyline integrated with Gimkit to enhance the critical thinking skills of fifth-grade elementary school students. This research employed a research and development (R&D) approach using the ADDIE model. The research subjects included two expert validators (a media expert and a subject-matter expert) and 21 fifth-grade students as trial participants. Data were collected through critical thinking skills tests, student response questionnaires, expert validation sheets, and teacher practicality assessment sheets. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis techniques, while quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. title: The The Effect of TPACK-Based Image Media on Students' Critical Thinking Ability
abstract: Critical thinking skills and the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework have become key issues in contemporary education, especially in Indonesia. Despite advancements in critical thinking education, the integration of technology remains a challenge. This study investigates the impact of TPACK-based image media on the development of students’ critical thinking skills in writing instruction. The research employs a quasi-experimental design using a post-test only, non-equivalent control group approach. The subjects include 5th grade students from two public elementary schools in the southern Surabaya area, comprising an experimental group (38 students) using TPACK-based image media and a control group (36 students) using traditional blackboard media. Data were collected through interviews, observations, document analysis, and tests. Statistical and inferential analyses were applied to assess the data. The findings reveal significant differences between the two groups, with students in the experimental group demonstrating superior critical thinking abilities. title: Role and Timing of Counselling in the Treatment of Severe Mental - Health Disorders: Implications for Counselling
abstract: Severe mental health disorders remain a global concern due to delayed treatment and the lack of optimal integration between pharmacological and psychosocial interventions, particularly regarding limited understanding of the appropriate role and timing of counseling in supporting long-term recovery. This study aims to analyze, evaluate, and synthesize the role and timing of counseling interventions. A qualitative approach with a conceptual–integrative design in the form of a position paper was employed. The study examined 45 scientific and policy documents, including peer-reviewed journal articles, clinical practice guidelines, reports from global health organizations, and empirical studies on pharmacological and psychosocial interventions. Data were collected through a document analysis method using a structured document analysis matrix as the research instrument, developed based on intervention focus, counseling timing, and recovery outcomes. Data analysis was conducted using thematic and comparative analysis to identify patterns, relationships, and conceptual gaps within the literature. abstract: The main issue is the lack of adequate resources and training for teachers, which affects the ability of curriculum developers to design effective strategies for both teachers and students. This study aims to examine the perspectives of curriculum developers on the obstacles encountered in the implementation of differentiated learning curriculum. The research uses a phenomenological method to explore information based on the direct experiences of curriculum developers. Data collection was conducted through in-depth interviews with 6 primary school teachers from the Penggerak School program. The collected data were analyzed using thematic analysis to identify key patterns emerging from their experiences. The results show that the integration of differentiated learning curriculum can be achieved through diagnostic assessment, teaching modules, or adjustments in teaching techniques by the teachers. title: In-depth Learning Policy Analysis in the Indonesian Education System with the SMART Approach
abstract: The Indonesian education system continues to face fundamental challenges, including low literacy outcomes, the dominance of rote learning, and disparities in teacher competency and distribution. This study aims to analyze the learning policy in depth using the SMART approach. This study employed a qualitative descriptive design with an evaluative approach, using the SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound) framework as its analytical lens. The research subjects consisted of official policy documents, curriculum guidelines, and academic literature on PM published between 2022 and 2025. Data were collected through document analysis, using a research instrument consisting of a document analysis sheet compiled based on the SMART framework. The results show that the PM policy is conceptually relevant to the demands of 21st-century education and is formulated with specific objectives. However, the policy lacks explicit quantitative indicators, measurable implementation targets, and a detailed operational roadmap. title: Problem-Based Learning E-LKPD to Improve Learning Outcomes in Pancasila Education
abstract: The key to successful learning lies in the availability of appropriate teaching materials, systematically arranged, and functioning as a guide in the learning process to achieve learning objectives. This study aims to describe the results of teacher and student needs analysis, and to test the validity, practicality, and effectiveness of problem-based learning (PBL) in improving learning outcomes of Pancasila Education in fifth-grade elementary school students. This study employs a Research and Development (R&D) approach, utilizing the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation) model. The research subjects consisted of 40 fifth-grade elementary school students selected through purposive sampling techniques. Data collection techniques included interviews, observations, and learning outcome tests. Data were analyzed quantitatively using descriptive statistics and inferential tests, and supported by qualitative analysis. title: Strengthening Local Culture through Informal Education in the Era of Society 5.0
abstract: In the era of Society 5.0, the preservation of local culture faces serious challenges due to the rapid flow of modernization and digitalization. This condition demands an adaptive value transmission strategy to prevent cultural identity from being eroded by developments. This study aims to analyze the role of informal education in strengthening local culture amidst the dynamics of modern society. The study used a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through participant observation, in-depth interviews with 15 informants, and documentation, and analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model. The subjects of this study were traditional leaders, village elders, parents, local youth, and participants in religious rituals. The results show that informal education takes place actively through family roles, involvement in traditional rituals, and intergenerational collaboration. Cultural values are inherited naturally through social practices without relying on the formal education system or digital technology.
